help.title: About Speech Studio
help.intro: Speech Studio voices text and recognises speech on your computer: the models run on your graphics card, and the cloud is used only where you turn it on.
how: Download the models on the first run: the studio picks the set for your graphics card.
Speech: write or paste a text, pick a voice and voice it.
Listening: open a recording, a link or the microphone and get the text with the speakers.
Save the result where you want it.
features: Voice cloning from a few seconds of a recording
Your own library of voices with photos and tags
Higgs Audio v3 locally, Drama 3 on cards from 6 GB
Speakers told apart in a recording
Cloud voices and recognition through OpenRouter and Google
An agent (MCP) drives the studio while you watch
sections: Listening: recognising speech and checking a voicing
Settings (⚙): models, cloud, network, agent, statistics
help.donateIntro: I build open-source software and do AI research. Most of what I create is free and available to everyone. Your donations help me keep creating and researching without worrying about where the next meal comes from =) Thank you 🙏

hub.why: How many people use Speech Studio and what for helps decide what to work on next. Nothing personal: no recordings, texts, voices or file names — only counts of jobs, which of the studio's functions were used (by name, never with what), the models each stage used, the version, a computer number shared by our programs (a one-way hash, not the system number itself), the graphics card class, how many seconds of speech were voiced in how many seconds of engine work, why a job failed, with paths, names and quoted text cut out on this computer before it is sent.
hub.byEnv: Turned off by DO_NOT_TRACK or STUDIO_TELEMETRY in the environment.
hub.nothing: Nothing is waiting to be sent today.
hub.feedNever: News have not been fetched from the server yet: the studio shows the news of its release.

tags.legend: Emotion, style, speed, pitch and expressiveness go to the start of the sentence; pause and sound go at the cursor. Right after a sound, with no space, write its onomatopoeia ("Ha-ha,", "Ahem,"): Higgs needs it. Tags the engine does not know are cut and named.
tags.universal: Pause and tempo work with any engine: tempo lasts to the next tempo tag or the end of the block. Select words, and the tempo covers only them.
tags.none: {{engine}} has no expression tags: pauses and tempo work.
tags.dramaRussian: Drama 3 tags and directions work poorly in Russian (checked by ear).
tags.legendDrama: An event goes at its place in the text; for a span, select the words and click. Drama reads the block’s direction as the delivery of the whole line.
tags.legendPlain: A tag goes at the cursor; tags the engine does not know are cut and named.
tags.qwen: Qwen3-TTS has no tags: write laughter and sounds as onomatopoeia in the text ("ha-ha", "hmm") and the model voices them by context; set the delivery in the direction (works with the model’s own voices, not with a clone).

hint.engine: The model that voices the whole project. A character or a block can have its own. Cloud engines are paid: the price shows before you start.
hint.lang: The language of the project's text: stress, how numbers are read and the check by ear depend on it. Auto lets the engine detect it.
hint.normalizeGroups: Which kinds of writing are read out as words. A group turned off stays in the text as written.
hint.sampling: How freely the model chooses the sound. Higher values sound livelier but fail more often; lower ones are steadier and flatter.
hint.seed: The starting number of randomness. Random makes every take sound new. Fixed makes the same text sound the same, handy for edits.
hint.qualityMode: Draft is fast and unchecked. Normal checks every take against its text. Best makes several takes, checks strictly and keeps the best.
hint.strictness: How many wrong words the check by ear allows. Strict allows almost none, lenient a word or two in a long sentence.
hint.leadIntoSilence: A line that does not fit its time first starts a little earlier, into the silence before it (up to a second), and only then speeds up.
hint.loudness: The finished file's loudness for where it goes: video, podcast or an ACX audiobook. Off keeps the model's level.
hint.blockLang: This passage's language when it differs from the project's: stress, numbers and voice follow this language.
hint.voiceFx: An effect over the voice: radio, phone, loudspeaker. It applies when you listen and export; the take itself stays clean.
hint.pauseAfter: The pause after the block in milliseconds. Empty follows the project's rules. Negative makes the next block interrupt this one.
hint.takes: Which of the block's takes sounds. The pin holds the chosen take: new voicing and checks will not replace it.
hint.voiceVariant: The same voice in another delivery: variants from the voice library.
hint.ownParams: Your own temperature and other sound settings instead of the shared ones: turn on and set values. Turn off to go back to the project's.
hint.abWith: Choose another take and switch with the A/B button: the sound goes on from the same moment, which makes comparing easier.
hint.direction: How to say this line: calmly, in a whisper, with a smile. Not every engine reads it; if yours does not, a warning shows.
hint.review: Your mark on the block. Approved locks the text and Voice all leaves it alone; Fix marks the block to be redone.
hint.howRead: How the engine will read the text: numbers as words, stress and dictionary rules. Here you can choose the stress of a doubtful word.
hint.tags: Tags for emotions and sounds (laugh, sigh, whisper) this block's engine understands. Click a tag to put it in the text at the cursor.
hint.wordNotes: A note on particular words: select them in the text and write what is wrong. It is not read aloud.
hint.ownRefWhole: On: the clip carries on into the block's speech and its intonation goes with it. Off: only the voice is taken from the clip.
hint.takeEdges: Move the take's start and end on the waveform: the cut does not change the file and can be undone.
hint.projectVoice: The default voice for every character and block without one of its own.
hint.castCard: This character's settings: their blocks use them unless a block has its own. Gender and age are what Pick voices goes by.
hint.allowDuration: Build the file even if some lines did not fit their subtitle time: they will run longer than they should.
hint.exportFormat: The file format. WAV and FLAC are lossless (FLAC is smaller), MP3, OGG and M4A are compressed, M4B is an audiobook with chapters.
hint.exportQuality: The file's sample rate, bit depth or bitrate. «As the format» uses the usual values for the chosen format.
hint.perBlock: Each block as a file of its own instead of one file, for editing or a game.
hint.packAudio: Put the voiced takes in the package too: it opens on another computer with the sound ready, but it gets bigger.
hint.newVoice: The voice for every block of the new project. Characters in a dialogue can get their own voices later.
hint.listenEngine: The recognition model for new recordings. Parakeet by default; for languages it does not know the studio takes CrisperWhisper by itself.
hint.listenLang: The language spoken in the recording. Auto lets the model detect it; if you know it, set it for better recognition.
hint.mic: A recording from the microphone becomes a Listening recording at once and is recognised. Choose the device on the right.
hint.watchFormats: The formats to save each recording's transcript in: subtitles (SRT, VTT, ASS), text (TXT) or everything with word times (JSON).
hint.withSpeakers: Mark who speaks: «Speaker 1:» or the name you gave the speaker.
hint.withTimes: Put the start time before each line of the text.
hint.listenSpeakers: How many people speak in the recording. Auto lets the model decide; if you know the number, set it and lines split between people more reliably.
hint.vad_threshold: How sure the model must be that a sound is speech, 0 to 1. Higher may lose quiet speech; lower lets noise in. Usually 0.5.
hint.vad_hysteresis: How far below the threshold the certainty must drop for speech to end. Larger keeps quiet word endings.
hint.vad_min_speech_ms: Sound shorter than this is not speech: clicks, coughs and knocks are dropped.
hint.vad_min_silence_ms: A pause shorter than this does not cut the speech: short breaths between words stay inside the piece.
hint.vad_pad_ms: A margin at the edges of each piece so the first and last sound of a word is not cut off.
hint.voiceGender: Who speaks in the reference. Pick voices matches characters by gender and age.
hint.voiceLang: The two-letter language code of the reference: ru, en, de. Voices are picked for characters of a project in that language by it.
hint.voiceTags: Your own words, comma-separated, for searching the library: calm, low, narrator.
hint.voiceSource: Where the voice came from: your recording, an archive, a site. Helps you recall whether you may use it.
hint.voiceConsent: Whether the voice's owner allowed cloning it. Someone else's voice without consent is for private experiments only.
hint.voiceLicense: The terms the voice recording may be used under, for example CC-BY-4.0. Empty means unknown.
hint.voiceVariantOf: Make this voice a delivery of another: the same person, another emotion. A block switches variants with one button.
hint.voiceCatalog: Open ready Russian voices from a cloud collection: listen and download the ones you need into the library.
hint.voicePack: Download a set of ready VibeVoice voices with their reference texts, to start without recordings of your own.
hint.voiceZipIn: Add voices from a ZIP: each voice's sound, reference text and card.
hint.voiceZipOut: Save the ticked voices to a ZIP with their cards and texts, to move them to another computer.
hint.cleanToggle: New voices are separated from music and noise as they are added. The original is kept.
hint.dictLang: The rule works only in text in this language. Any means in all.
hint.dictVoice: The rule works only for this voice: handy when one voice gets a word wrong and the others do not.
hint.musicWhere: Which book track the song goes on. New track makes a separate one with its own volume.
hint.musicAt: The second of the book where the song starts. Empty puts it right after the track's last clip.
hint.designDescription: What the voice should be: gender, age, timbre, manner. The model understands a description in English or Chinese best.
hint.designSample: The line the candidates will say. It becomes the reference text of the saved voice, so write it in the language you need.
hint.designCount: How many different voices to make from one description, to pick the best. Each is a separate generation.
hint.podcastSpeakers: The hosts' names and each one's manner: the model writes their lines in that manner, and the names become the project's characters.
hint.podcastMinutes: The podcast's rough length. It decides how many lines the model writes.
hint.listenSpeakersBar: Who speaks in the recording. A corrected name goes into the export. The buttons beside hide the speaker's lines, make a voice of them and remember them for other recordings.
hint.assistantLlm: The language model that helps with the text: expression tags and punctuation, casting a book by roles, writing a podcast.

talk.title: Live
talk.hint: An agent connected over MCP hears you through the microphone and answers aloud as it writes. Speak over it to interrupt.
talk.connect: Connect an agent to the studio:
talk.ask: Then ask it: “talk with me by voice through Speech Studio”.
talk.micOnHint: The studio listens to the microphone: every phrase you end with a pause goes to the agent.
talk.micOffHint: Ends the conversation; it stays a recording in Listening.
talk.silenceHint: Cuts the agent off now, as speaking over it does.
talk.historyHint: Shows or hides the conversation as text.
talk.widgetHint: Open Live as a small bar over every other window. The sound plays here.
talk.muteHint: Pause: the agent stops talking and does not hear you. Press again to go on with the conversation.
talk.outputNamesHint: The browser names speakers only after you allow the microphone.
talk.outputUnsupported: This browser cannot choose the speaker.
talk.speakToTest: Say something: the bar should move.
talk.parakeetLang: Parakeet picks the language itself and may write some words in another one; to keep to the language set here, choose Nemotron 3.5.

mic.offHint: Turn the microphone off. Only the person turns it on, with a button in the studio; with no studio window open it turns off by itself.
